subject: MediaWave — proposed hosted commit uplift & rate-limit ops details
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.ai>
To: Claire D'Souza <claire@mediawave.io>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-09-27T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal window + recommended hosted commit uplift

Hi Claire —

Hope you had a good weekend. Renewal for MediaWave's Hosted API subscription comes up in mid-November and I wanted to open the conversation early so we can align on capacity and pricing before your Q4 campaign ramps.

High level: your app's 90-day token consumption shows sustained growth (see Q3 snapshot attached). Given the traffic profile — nightly batch inference plus daytime burst windows — we recommend moving from your current 2M token/month commit to a 6M commit with a 3x burst allowance and a 12-month term. That buys a lower unit price and guaranteed throughput during your peak windows.

Questions I have for you now:
- Are you expecting any new feature launches before December that would materially increase average sequence length?
- Any procurement or approval windows we should be aware of?

I'll loop in Monica (CS) to confirm operational readiness and Karthik for throughput/runbook items. I've attached a first-pass proposal and the usage CSV for reference.

If helpful we can book a 30-min call this week to walk the proposal line-by-line.

Thanks —
Sean Gallagher
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
sean@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0143

Attachment: mediawave_commit_proposal_v1.pdf
Attachment: usage_report_q3.csv

From: Claire D'Souza <claire@mediawave.io>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.ai>
Cc: MediaWave Procurement <procurement@mediawave.io>
Date: 2028-09-28T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal window + recommended hosted commit uplift

Hi Sean —

Thanks for the heads-up and for the usage snapshot — helpful. A few quick notes from our side:

- We are planning a new personalization rollout in November that will increase average tokens per request by ~20–30% for the first two weeks after launch.
- Procurement has a standard 60-day review window and they will need the new order form by Oct 10 to hit a Nov 15 start date.

Specific asks:
1) Can you confirm how burst credits work if we exceed the 6M commit in a single month? Is there an automatic overage billing or do you throttle at rate limits?
2) We need a separate SLA for latency during our US peak (PST 17:00–21:00). Can Redwood guarantee p50/p95 numbers for the proposed commit tier?
3) Any additional discounts for seats/consumption if we sign a 24-month term vs 12?

If possible, Monica — can you share an ops checklist for switching to the higher commit (KV cache prewarming, key rotations, any downtime windows)?

I'll be available for a call on Friday morning PT.

Best,
Claire D'Souza
Senior Product Manager, MediaWave
claire@mediawave.io

Team — forwarding Claire's reply. She called out three things we need to answer for procurement: burst behavior, SLA numbers for the tier, and term discounting.

Notes / ask:
- Karthik: can you put together a brief note about rate-limits vs overage billing, and what we can guarantee for sustained burst windows (3x burst allowance in the proposal). Also include any KV-cache prewarm steps for a zero-downtime lift.
- Monica: please attach the ops checklist Claire requested and any runbook we would hand over for the rollout.
- Ben: procurement is asking about 24-month pricing. Can you run a scenario for 12 vs 24 months at 6M/month and one at 9M/month? We should be explicit about any committed discount vs on-demand.

Claire — looping you in so you can see internal owners. We'll aim to respond with a consolidated proposal by Tue EOD so you have time for your Oct 10 procurement window.

Thanks,
Sean

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Cc: Claire D'Souza <claire@mediawave.io>
Date: 2028-10-01T09:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Renewal window + recommended hosted commit uplift — ops + rate notes

Hi all — quick technical summary for the proposal (TL;DR below).

Burst and overage model
- Proposal: 6M/month commit + 3x burst window (usable up to 18M in a month). Bursts are allowed up to the allowance; sustained usage beyond the 3x burst in a single month triggers standard overage billing at 1.25x the committed unit rate. We do not silently throttle at the token-level for committed customers; instead, we prefer controlled overage to avoid request failures.

Rate-limits & throughput guarantees
- For the 6M commit tier on our US-hosted fleet, we can guarantee the following SLOs during your specified PST peak (17:00–21:00): p50 latency < 120ms, p95 latency < 420ms for 1–2k concurrent connections with typical request lengths (<=1k tokens).
- If MediaWave expects >2k concurrent connections in peak windows, we recommend the 9M commit with a dedicated throughput reservation to keep p95 under 300ms.

Ops checklist (short)
- KV cache warm-up: run a 48-hour controlled replay at 20% traffic to populate prefix caches — no downtime.
- Key rotation: no in-band downtime; provide new keys 48 hours before cutover and coordinate cutover during low-traffic window.
- Routing: we recommend pinning the production service to US-west nodes during the first 2 weeks after launch.

Attachments: small runbook excerpt included below and I'll attach a prepared order form for Ben to incorporate pricing.

TL;DR: 6M commit + 3x burst works for your expected November rollout if you accept overage billing at 1.25x after burst allowance; move to 9M if you expect concurrent connections >2k.

—Karthik
Principal Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment (referenced): usage_runbook_excerpt.txt

From: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.ai>
To: Claire D'Souza <claire@mediawave.io>, MediaWave Procurement <procurement@mediawave.io>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-10-02T16:42:00-07:00
Subject: Final proposal & next steps — MediaWave hosted commit uplift

Claire — thanks for the rapid turnaround and for flagging procurement timelines. Summary and next steps below.

Summary proposal (as discussed):
- Term: 12 months (option to extend to 24 with additional 6% committed discount).
- Commit: 6,000,000 tokens/month.
- Burst allowance: up to 3x monthly commit (18M tokens) in any single month.
- Overage: billable at 1.25x committed unit rate beyond burst allowance.
- SLA: p50 <120ms, p95 <420ms during PST 17:00–21:00 for <=2k concurrent connections. 9M commit recommended for >2k concurrency to maintain p95 <300ms.
- Ops: KV cache warm-up 48-hr replay, no downtime; key rotation window 48 hours pre-cutover; recommended US-west node pinning for first two weeks.

Attachments and links: amended order form attached; DocuSign link below for the 12-month order. Also included the Q3 usage CSV for your finance team.

Next steps:
1) Procurement: review amended_order_form_2028-10-02.docx and return any redlines by Oct 6.
2) Ops: Monica will schedule an ops handoff call for Oct 9 to walk the runbook and KV cache plan.
3) Sign: We will issue the DocuSign envelope once procurement confirms no material redlines.

If the team prefers a 24-month term, Ben will circulate the 24-month figure (6% additional discount) in an updated order form today EOD.

Thanks everyone — happy to hop on a call if any of this needs clarification.

Best,
Sean Gallagher
